title: Isaiah Chapter 26 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 26 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 26 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 26.

questions.question: In Isaiah 26, what is described as a strong city appointed with salvation for walls and bulwarks?
questions.correctAnswer: The land of Judah
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:1 states that in that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah, which is described as having a strong city with salvation appointed for walls and bulwarks.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 26, who is allowed to enter when the gates are opened?
options: The righteous nation which keepeth the truth
questions.correctAnswer: The righteous nation which keepeth the truth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:2 instructs to open the gates so that the righteous nation which keeps the truth may enter in.

questions.question: Who does God keep in perfect peace according to Isaiah 26?
options: Those whose mind is stayed on Him because they trust in Him
questions.correctAnswer: Those whose mind is stayed on Him because they trust in Him
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:3 says that God will keep in perfect peace those whose mind is stayed on Him because they trust in Him.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 26 commands us to trust in the LORD for everlasting strength.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:4 says to trust in the LORD forever, for in the LORD JEHOVAH is everlasting strength.

questions.question: What does the LORD do to the lofty city, according to Isaiah 26?
options: He lays it low even to the ground, bringing it to dust
questions.correctAnswer: He lays it low even to the ground, bringing it to dust
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:5 states that the LORD brings down those who dwell on high and lays the lofty city low even to the ground, bringing it to dust.

questions.question: Who will tread down the lofty city as mentioned in Isaiah 26?
options: The feet of the poor and the steps of the needy
questions.correctAnswer: The feet of the poor and the steps of the needy
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:6 says the foot shall tread down the lofty city, even the feet of the poor and the steps of the needy.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 26, how is the way of the just described?
questions.correctAnswer: Uprightness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:7 states that the way of the just is uprightness.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 26 says the LORD weighs the path of the just.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:7 notes that the LORD, who is most upright, weighs the path of the just.

questions.question: In Isaiah 26, what is the desire of the soul in waiting for the LORD?
options: To remember the name and judgments of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: To remember the name and judgments of the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:8 explains that in the way of the LORD's judgments, they wait for Him and the desire of their soul is to His name and remembrance.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 26 says the inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness when the LORD's judgments are in the earth.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:9 states that when the LORD's judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness.

questions.question: Who does Isaiah 26 say will not learn righteousness even if favor is shown to them?
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:10 says that even if favor is shown to the wicked, they will not learn righteousness.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 26, what will happen to the fire of the LORD's enemies?
questions.correctAnswer: It will devour them
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:11 says the fire of the LORD's enemies shall devour them.

questions.question: In Isaiah 26, who is said to have dominion over the people before the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Other lords
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:13 mentions that other lords besides the LORD have had dominion over the people.

questions.question: Which event happens first in Isaiah 26?
options: The LORD bringing down the lofty city
The righteous nation entering through opened gates
The LORD ordaining peace for the people
The dead men arising and singing
questions.correctAnswer: The righteous nation entering through opened gates
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:2 commands opening the gates for the righteous nation to enter, which occurs before the LORD brings down the lofty city (verse 5), ordains peace (verse 12), and the dead arising (verse 19).

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 26 describes God's people as waiting in the way of His judgments.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:8 states that in the way of God's judgments, His people have waited for Him.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 26 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 26 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 26:8, what is the desire of the soul directed towards?
questions.correctAnswer: God's name and remembrance
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:8 states that the desire of the soul is to God's name and to the remembrance of Him, emphasizing the longing for God's presence and justice.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 26:9 describe the attitude of the speaker toward seeking God?
options: With the soul in the night and spirit early
questions.correctAnswer: With the soul in the night and spirit early
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:9 shows a deep, continuous desire to seek God both night and early morning, demonstrating persistent faith and devotion.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 26:10 say about the wicked when shown favor?
questions.correctAnswer: They do not learn righteousness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:10 indicates that even when favor is shown to the wicked, they do not learn righteousness but continue to act unjustly.

questions.question: What will happen to those who envy God's people, according to Isaiah 26:11?
options: They shall be ashamed and devoured by fire
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be ashamed and devoured by fire
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:11 states that those who envy God's people will see and be ashamed, and the fire of God's enemies will devour them, showing divine justice.

questions.question: What peace does the LORD ordain for His people as described in Isaiah 26:12?
options: Peace because He has wrought their works
questions.correctAnswer: Peace because He has wrought their works
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:12 explains that the LORD ordains peace for His people because He has worked all their works in them, emphasizing God's sovereign involvement.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 26:13, why do the people mention only the LORD's name?
options: Because other lords had dominion but only the LORD is acknowledged
Because the LORD is the richest
questions.correctAnswer: Because other lords had dominion but only the LORD is acknowledged
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:13 points out that although other lords had control over them, the people choose to mention only the LORD's name, showing exclusive devotion.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 26:14 teach about the fate of those who have opposed God?
options: They are dead and shall not rise again
questions.correctAnswer: They are dead and shall not rise again
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:14 declares that those who opposed God are dead and shall not live again, emphasizing the finality of divine judgment.

questions.question: How does the passage in Isaiah 26:8-9 show the relationship between waiting on God's judgments and learning righteousness?
options: Waiting on God's judgments leads inhabitants to learn righteousness
Waiting on God's judgments leads to despair
Ignoring God's judgments results in righteousness
God's judgments have no effect on righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: Waiting on God's judgments leads inhabitants to learn righteousness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:8 expresses waiting for God's judgments, and verse 9 explains that when God's judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants will learn righteousness, showing the connection between patient faith and moral growth.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 26:10 suggest about the character of the wicked even when living in a land of uprightness?
options: They deal unjustly and ignore the majesty of the LORD
They immediately repent and live righteously
They become leaders of the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: They deal unjustly and ignore the majesty of the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:10 highlights the stubbornness of the wicked who, even in a land of uprightness, continue to act unjustly and do not recognize God's majesty.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 26:11 states that when the LORD's hand is lifted up, all will see and obey immediately.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:11 says that when the LORD's hand is lifted up, some will not see, but eventually they will see and be ashamed for their envy, indicating delayed realization rather than immediate obedience.

questions.question: Based on Isaiah 26:12-13, how should believers respond to past dominion by other lords?
options: By acknowledging only the LORD and making mention of His name
By seeking alliances with other lords
By relying on their own strength
questions.correctAnswer: By acknowledging only the LORD and making mention of His name
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:13 shows that despite other lords having dominion, believers should honor and mention only the LORD's name, reflecting faithfulness and loyalty.

questions.question: What metaphor does Isaiah 26:17 use to describe the pain and struggle of the people?
options: A woman with child drawing near to delivery
A tree bending in the wind
questions.correctAnswer: A woman with child drawing near to delivery
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:17 compares the people's suffering to a woman in labor pains, illustrating intense struggle and anticipation.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 26:18 says the people have brought forth deliverance and the inhabitants have fallen.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:18 states that the people have brought forth wind and have not wrought any deliverance, nor have the inhabitants fallen, indicating frustration and lack of success.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 26:19, what will happen to the dead men and the speaker's dead body?
options: They shall remain in the dust forever
questions.correctAnswer: They shall live and arise
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:19 declares that the dead shall live again and arise, symbolizing resurrection and hope beyond death.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 26:14 teaches that the memory of the dead enemies will endure forever.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:14 explains that God has visited and destroyed the enemies and made all their memory to perish, meaning their memory will not endure.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 26 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 26.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 26:15, what has the LORD done to the nation?
options: Increased the nation and glorified Himself
Destroyed the nation and scattered its people
Ignored the nation and left it in despair
Punished the nation for its sins
questions.correctAnswer: Increased the nation and glorified Himself
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:15 states that the LORD has increased the nation and is glorified, showing His sovereign power over the people.

questions.question: In Isaiah 26:16, how did the people respond when they were in trouble?
options: They poured out a prayer to the LORD
They sought help from other gods
questions.correctAnswer: They poured out a prayer to the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:16 describes that in trouble, the people visited the LORD and poured out prayers when chastening was upon them.

questions.question: What simile does Isaiah use in verse 17 to describe the people's suffering?
options: A woman with child near delivery in pain
A tree bending in the storm
A traveler lost in the desert
questions.correctAnswer: A woman with child near delivery in pain
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:17 compares the people's suffering to that of a woman in labor, emphasizing the intensity and imminence of their pain.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 26:18 say about the outcome of the people's labor and pain?
options: They have not wrought any deliverance and the inhabitants have not fallen
They have achieved great victory and peace
They have built new cities and prospered
They have forgotten their troubles and rejoiced
questions.correctAnswer: They have not wrought any deliverance and the inhabitants have not fallen
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:18 laments that despite their pains, it is as if they brought forth wind, with no deliverance accomplished and no fall of inhabitants.

questions.question: Isaiah 26:19 speaks of the dead rising. Which New Testament passage echoes this theme of resurrection?
options: John 5:28-29 about the resurrection of the dead
questions.correctAnswer: John 5:28-29 about the resurrection of the dead
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:19's promise that the dead shall live is echoed in John 5:28-29, where Jesus speaks of the resurrection at the last day.

questions.question: What instruction does Isaiah give in verse 20 concerning the people during indignation?
options: Enter chambers, shut doors, and hide for a little moment
Go out and fight the enemies
Build new walls around the city
questions.correctAnswer: Enter chambers, shut doors, and hide for a little moment
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:20 advises the people to take refuge inside their chambers and wait until the LORD's indignation passes.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 26:21, why does the LORD come out of his place?
options: To punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity
To bless the people with peace
To gather the faithful into His kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: To punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:21 explains that the LORD comes forth to punish the earth's inhabitants because of their sin.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Isaiah 26:19 where the dead are described as arising and singing?
options: Personification of the earth and the dead
questions.correctAnswer: Personification of the earth and the dead
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:19 personifies the earth as casting out the dead and the dead as awakening and singing, illustrating resurrection vividly.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated 'indignation' in Isaiah 26:20, and what does it imply about God's judgment?
options: Anger or wrath, implying a temporary but intense divine punishment
questions.correctAnswer: Anger or wrath, implying a temporary but intense divine punishment
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'indignation' (חֵמָה, chemah) conveys God's wrath or anger, suggesting a fierce but limited judgment as seen in Isaiah 26:20.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 26:18’s description of 'bringing forth wind' serve as a typology for spiritual barrenness?
options: It symbolizes fruitless efforts and lack of true deliverance
It represents the wind of the Holy Spirit
It describes a literal storm affecting the land
It signifies the beginning of a new covenant
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes fruitless efforts and lack of true deliverance
questions.explanation: The phrase 'brought forth wind' in Isaiah 26:18 typifies futile labor without productive results, indicating spiritual barrenness.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book shares a thematic connection with Isaiah 26:19 regarding resurrection and awakening of the dead?
options: Daniel 12:2 speaks of many awakening to everlasting life or shame
Leviticus 16 about the Day of Atonement
Joshua 6 about the fall of Jericho
questions.correctAnswer: Daniel 12:2 speaks of many awakening to everlasting life or shame
questions.explanation: Daniel 12:2 echoes Isaiah 26:19 in its teaching about resurrection and awakening of the dead to life or judgment.

questions.question: In Isaiah 26:21, the phrase 'the earth shall disclose her blood' most likely refers to what historical or theological concept?
options: The revelation of hidden injustices and judgment for bloodshed
The cleansing of the land by rainfall
The earth shaking during an earthquake
questions.correctAnswer: The revelation of hidden injustices and judgment for bloodshed
questions.explanation: The phrase metaphorically indicates that the earth will reveal the blood of the slain, symbolizing God’s judgment on hidden crimes as per Isaiah 26:21.

questions.question: Which New Testament event does Isaiah 26:19’s resurrection imagery foreshadow?
options: The resurrection of Jesus Christ and the future general resurrection
The baptism of Jesus in the Jordan River
The Pentecost outpouring of the Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: The resurrection of Jesus Christ and the future general resurrection
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:19’s depiction of the dead rising prefigures the resurrection of Christ and the general resurrection described in the New Testament.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 26:16 suggests that prayer is only effective when there is no chastening or trouble.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:16 states that people poured out prayers when chastening was upon them, showing prayer during trouble is effective.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 26:4 encourages trusting in the LORD forever because in Him is everlasting strength.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:4 explicitly instructs to trust in the LORD forever, for He is everlasting strength.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 26 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 26 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Isaiah 26:3 regarding the believer whose mind is steadfast on God?
questions.correctAnswer: God's perfect peace
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:3 explicitly states that God will keep in perfect peace the one whose mind is stayed on Him because he trusts in God, highlighting the attribute of God's sustaining peace.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 26:5-6, what happens to the 'lofty city' and what does this reveal about God's justice?
options: It is exalted to a higher place to protect the righteous
It is humbled to the dust, showing God opposes the proud
It is destroyed by foreign armies as a punishment
It is preserved by God's mercy for future generations
questions.correctAnswer: It is humbled to the dust, showing God opposes the proud
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:5-6 teaches that God brings down the lofty city to the dust, indicating His opposition to pride and the exalted who oppose Him, demonstrating divine justice against arrogance.

questions.question: What doctrine is taught by the declaration in Isaiah 26:14 that 'they are dead, they shall not live; they are deceased, they shall not rise'?
options: Finality of death for the ungodly
questions.correctAnswer: Finality of death for the ungodly
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:14 declares that the dead will not rise again, teaching the doctrine that those opposed to God will face a final, irreversible death, consistent with the doctrine of eternal separation from God.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 26:19 contribute to the biblical doctrine of resurrection?
options: It affirms the dead will live and arise
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms the dead will live and arise
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:19 explicitly states that the dead shall live and arise, affirming the doctrine of bodily resurrection of the righteous, a key hope in biblical eschatology.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth is revealed by synthesizing Isaiah 26:3 and Isaiah 26:4 regarding the believer's trust in God?
options: Trust in God leads to perfect peace and eternal strength
Trust in God guarantees earthly riches and power
Trust in God results in absence of suffering
Trust in God ensures exemption from judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in God leads to perfect peace and eternal strength
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:3 promises perfect peace for those who trust God, and 26:4 asserts that in the LORD is everlasting strength, together teaching that reliance on God grants both peace and enduring strength.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 26:7 reveal about the nature of God's judgment in relation to human righteousness?
options: God judges arbitrarily without regard to actions
God weighs the path of the just with perfect uprightness
God ignores the deeds of the righteous
God rewards only those without sin
questions.correctAnswer: God weighs the path of the just with perfect uprightness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:7 states that God, described as most upright, weighs the path of the just, showing that divine judgment is perfectly just and discerning concerning human righteousness.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 26:21 express God's role in final judgment and the moral accountability of the earth's inhabitants?
options: God will overlook the sins of the earth
God will come forth to punish iniquity and expose bloodshed
The earth will hide the slain forever
God will delay judgment until all repent
questions.correctAnswer: God will come forth to punish iniquity and expose bloodshed
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:21 clearly states the LORD will come out to punish the inhabitants for their sins, and the earth will disclose the bloodshed, emphasizing God's righteous judgment and moral accountability.

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by combining Isaiah 26:12 and Isaiah 26:13 about God's sovereignty and the worship due to Him alone?
options: God shares dominion with other gods but is the strongest
God ordains peace and is the only true Lord to be worshiped
Human works are independent of God's will
Other gods have equal dominion alongside the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains peace and is the only true Lord to be worshiped
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:12 acknowledges God ordains peace and works in us, while 26:13 affirms that although other lords had dominion, only God is truly to be named and worshiped, underscoring God's unique sovereignty.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that divine justice is inconsistent because the wicked sometimes prosper. What does Isaiah 26:10 teach about the wicked and their learning of righteousness?
options: The wicked always learn righteousness quickly
The wicked will not learn righteousness even if favored
The wicked are always punished immediately
The wicked are never shown favor
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked will not learn righteousness even if favored
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:10 explains that even if favor is shown to the wicked, they will not learn righteousness, addressing sceptical claims by emphasizing the stubbornness of sin despite apparent prosperity.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 26:17-18 metaphorically illustrate about the spiritual condition of the people in relation to their deliverance?
options: The people are joyful and fully delivered
The people are in painful travail but have not produced deliverance
The people have given birth to many righteous deeds
The people are indifferent to God's work
questions.correctAnswer: The people are in painful travail but have not produced deliverance
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:17-18 uses the metaphor of a woman in labor who only brings forth wind, indicating the people's painful efforts without actual deliverance, highlighting spiritual barrenness despite suffering.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection to redemption is highlighted by Isaiah 26:19’s promise of resurrection combined with Isaiah 26:20’s call for the people to hide until indignation passes?
options: The final judgment will not affect God's people
The resurrection of the dead and protection during God's wrath anticipates ultimate redemption
God's people will be destroyed alongside sinners
The resurrection is only spiritual, not bodily
questions.correctAnswer: The resurrection of the dead and protection during God's wrath anticipates ultimate redemption
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:19 promises the dead will arise, and 26:20 instructs God's people to hide until His wrath passes, together portraying God’s redemptive plan involving resurrection and preservation during judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Isaiah 26:15 where God is praised for increasing the nation and being glorified to the ends of the earth?
options: God's omnipotence in expansion and glory
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipotence in expansion and glory
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:15 highlights God's power to increase the nation and His glory spreading to the earth's ends, emphasizing God's omnipotence and sovereign majesty.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is taught by the plea in Isaiah 26:2 for the gates to be opened to the righteous nation that keeps the truth?
options: The doctrine of salvation by works
The doctrine of sanctification and entrance into God's kingdom
The doctrine of predestination excluding the righteous
The doctrine of universal access regardless of righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of sanctification and entrance into God's kingdom
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:2 connects the opening of gates to the entry of the righteous who keep the truth, teaching the doctrine that sanctification and truthfulness are necessary for entering God's kingdom.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Isaiah 26:11 and Isaiah 26:6 convey about the fate of God's enemies and the role of the humble in God's judgment?
options: God's enemies will be victorious over the humble
The humble will trample the proud enemies who are devoured by fire
God's enemies will be exalted and the poor defeated
The poor and needy will be judged alongside the proud
questions.correctAnswer: The humble will trample the proud enemies who are devoured by fire
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:6 describes the feet of the poor treading down the lofty city, while 26:11 says the fire of God's enemies will devour them, together teaching that God exalts the humble and punishes the proud enemies.

questions.question: What is revealed about prayer and affliction in Isaiah 26:16?
options: The people ignore God during trouble
The people earn salvation through their prayers
The people earnestly seek God and pour out prayers during chastening
Prayer is unnecessary as God's will is fixed
questions.correctAnswer: The people earnestly seek God and pour out prayers during chastening
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26:16 shows that in times of trouble and chastening, the people visit God and pour out prayers, revealing the doctrine of prayer as a response to divine discipline.
